channel.title: EngineerzCorneR — Posts
channel.description: Deep-dive technical write-ups across Electrical, Mechanical, HVAC, Automation, Civil and Solar.

item.title: Beam Bending Basics: Why Section Modulus Decides Capacity, Not Just Load
item.description: Why a beam's bending capacity comes down to two separate checks — bending stress against section modulus, and deflection against span — not just the applied load.

item.title: Busbar Sizing: Why the Short-Circuit Check Often Governs, Not the Continuous Rating
item.description: Busbar cross-section from continuous current rating, then checked against short-circuit thermal withstand and electrodynamic force.

item.title: Duct Sizing: Why Velocity Limits Matter as Much as Airflow
item.description: Sizing ductwork for airflow, velocity and circular-equivalent diameter, and why designing for velocity limits matters as much as hitting the required airflow figure.

item.title: Earned Value Management: Reading Project Health From Three Numbers
item.description: Why 'on budget' and 'on schedule' need separate proof, what Planned Value, Earned Value and Actual Cost each measure.

item.title: Earthing & Grounding Systems Explained: Why Resistance Is the Whole Game
item.description: What an earthing system is actually protecting against, why grid resistance is the number that matters, the factors that drive it.

item.title: Electrical Panel Factory Acceptance Test (FAT): The Complete Checklist
item.description: The 8 stages of an LV panel FAT — visual and mechanical inspection, insulation resistance, hi-pot, functional, protection and interlock tests, and documentation — plus the acceptance criteria that close it out.

item.title: MCB, MCCB, ACB, RCCB & More: Electrical Switchgear & Protection Devices Explained
item.description: MCB, MCCB, ACB, VCB, SF6 breakers, RCCB, RCBO, ELCB, isolators, contactors, relays, fuses, SPDs and busbars — what each device does, how it differs, and where it's used.

item.title: What Is an ELV System? Types, Components & the BIM Engineer's Role
item.description: Extra Low Voltage systems explained: the six categories, how ELV differs from electrical power systems, and where MEP BIM fits in.

item.title: Erosional vs. Economic Velocity: Which One Actually Sizes Your Pipe?
item.description: Two different velocity limits compete to size a process line — economic velocity minimizes lifecycle cost, the API RP 14E erosional velocity protects the pipe wall. The lower of the two always governs.

item.title: Facility & Property Management: Key Codes & Standards Reference
item.description: The key codes and standards that govern facility and property management — maintenance, HVAC, fire & life safety, occupational health, electrical, building codes, and more.

item.title: Facility Management: Monthly Invoice Processing
item.description: How FM teams process monthly invoices — the 3 expense categories (utility, service, consumables), the 10-step verification-to-filing workflow, and a worked invoice tracker example.

item.title: FM-200, Novec 1230, CO2 & Foam: Fire Suppression Systems Explained
item.description: FM-200, Novec 1230, CO2 and foam fire suppression systems compared — components, applications, discharge time, ozone depletion and global warming potential, plus which NFPA standard applies to each.

item.title: Flame Retardant vs Flame Resistant Cables: Know the Difference
item.description: IEC 60332 vs IEC 60331 explained — why flame retardant cables stop fire from spreading while flame (fire) resistant cables keep circuits alive during a fire.

item.title: Gas Insulated Substation (GIS) Explained
item.description: A GIS packs busbars, breakers, disconnects, earthing switches and transformers into a sealed, SF6-filled metal enclosure — 10-20% the footprint of a conventional air-insulated substation. Key components, why it's used, and where.

item.title: Grade & Slope: Why Percent, Ratio and Degrees Aren't the Same Number
item.description: How rise over run converts between percent grade, a ratio like 1:20, and an angle in degrees — and why mixing up the three is a common site-drawing mistake.

item.title: Harmonics in Power Systems: Sources, Effects and How to Mitigate Them
item.description: Where harmonics come from, how IEEE 519 limits voltage THD at the point of common coupling, what unmanaged harmonics do to cables, transformers and capacitors.

item.title: Current THD and K-Factor: Why Harmonic Distortion Derates Your Transformer
item.description: How current THD and K-factor are calculated from a harmonic spectrum, why K-factor weights higher harmonics more heavily.

item.title: Heat Pump Sizing Basics: Why Electrification Made This a Core Skill
item.description: Why heat pump sizing isn't the same exercise as furnace or AC sizing, what COP and capacity-at-temperature actually mean.

item.title: HIRA vs. JSA vs. SOP: Which Safety Document Do You Actually Need?
item.description: HIRA, JSA and SOP all show up in the same industrial safety training deck, but they operate at three different scopes and points in time — whole-workplace planning, one specific job before it starts, and the daily standard method once it's running.

item.title: How to Select a Digital Protection Relay
item.description: A step-by-step working method for selecting a digital protection relay — from identifying the protected equipment through CT/VT matching, I/O sizing.

item.title: HVAC MEP Thumb Rules & Formulas: Quick Reference for Engineers
item.description: Preliminary-design thumb rules for cooling load, airflow, fan and pump power, chilled water flow, chiller capacity, cooling tower sizing, and pipe sizing — with the formula behind each one.

item.title: HVAC & Plumbing Default Design Values: The Quick Reference
item.description: Common default design values for HVAC and plumbing — duct and pipe velocities, pressure drops, ACH, noise criteria, fresh air rates, temperatures, and plumbing velocities, pressures and slopes — for a first-pass sizing check.

item.title: HVAC System Components Explained
item.description: How an HVAC system actually conditions a space, component by component — compressor, condenser, expansion device, evaporator, air handler, ductwork, and controls.

item.title: Icw, Icu, Ics & Icm Explained: Four kA Ratings, Four Different Jobs
item.description: Four short-circuit kA ratings on a breaker or busbar nameplate — Icw, Icu, Ics and Icm — and what each one actually certifies, with a worked example showing how they relate.

item.title: IEC 104 Communication Protocol Explained
item.description: What IEC 60870-5-104 actually does, how it extends IEC 101 over TCP/IP, the master-slave request/response and spontaneous-reporting model, a security reference, and where it's used in SCADA and remote control systems.

item.title: IECEx / ATEX Zones vs NEC Class & Division: Hazardous Area Classification
item.description: How the IEC 60079 / ATEX Zone system (Zone 0/1/2, 20/21/22) compares to the North American NEC Class & Division system — equivalency table, gas/dust groups, temperature classes and Ex protection types explained.

item.title: Ingress Protection (IP) Ratings Explained
item.description: How an IP rating is actually built — the solid-protection digit, the liquid-protection digit, and the optional letters — decoded digit by digit against IEC 60529, with a full ratings reference and an IP-to-NEMA cross-check.

item.title: IS, IEC & IEEE Codes: The Standards Behind Electrical Engineering
item.description: What IS, IEC and IEEE standards each actually govern, a working reference list across wiring, earthing, transformers, switchgear and solar PV.

item.title: Junction Boxes Explained: Types, Parts & Ratings
item.description: What a junction box actually does, the main types — pull box, gang box, weatherproof, explosion-proof, conduit body, terminal box, panel enclosure — its parts, a material and rating reference, box-fill sizing, and a selection checklist.

item.title: K-Rated Transformers: What K-Factor Means and When You Need One
item.description: What a K-rated transformer actually is, the IEEE C57.110 K-factor scale from K-1 to K-20, how it differs in construction from a standard transformer.
